Simulate 2D natural convection in a square cavity using the OpenFOAM solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam with the Boussinesq approximation.
The domain is a 1 m by 1 m square cavity in the x-y plane, with a single cell in the z direction to enforce 2D behavior.
The mesh is a uniform 80 x 80 cell block in x and y (81 x 81 nodes), with no local refinement.
The fluid is air at a reference temperature of 295 K, using real physical properties: kinematic viscosity nu = 1.57e-5 m^2/s, thermal diffusivity alpha = 2.22e-5 m^2/s, thermal expansion coefficient beta = 1/295 1/K, and base density rho = 1.184 kg/m^3.
Gravity is a uniform body force g = (0, -9.81, 0) m/s^2 acting in the negative y direction.
The left wall (x = 0) has a fixedValue temperature of 300 K and a noSlip velocity condition.
The right wall (x = 1) has a fixedValue temperature of 290 K and a noSlip velocity condition.
The top wall (y = 1) has a zeroGradient temperature condition (adiabatic) and a noSlip velocity condition.
The bottom wall (y = 0) has a zeroGradient temperature condition (adiabatic) and a noSlip velocity condition.
The initial temperature field is uniform at 295 K everywhere in the domain.
The initial velocity field is zero everywhere in the domain.
The simulation runs transiently with an adjustable time step until the solution reaches steady state, indicated by time-independent residuals and negligible change in field values between consecutive time steps.
No Ra target is imposed; the resulting Rayleigh number is whatever the specified geometry, temperature difference, and real air properties produce.
